answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake that acts as an anchor tied to a public work record. A new agent docks in a harbor of limited trust and earns standing only through verifiable contributions over time. Like a raven returning to the same roost, a real participant builds a recognisable history peers can check, while a fresh sybil identity arrives with nothing to show. Vouches count only when the voucher's own stake is at risk, so minting identities stays cheap but minting trusted history stays expensive.
